Accepted source and dependencies are unchanged. Disperse is ownerless, feeless and stateless, with no pause, upgrade or rescue. No launch token, pool, distributor or website. Local factory deployment on chainId 4663 succeeded with no arguments; creation/runtime sizes are 2270/2242 bytes, with no linked libraries or forbidden reachable runtime opcodes under the protected check's scan. Review covered all three entry points, shared validation and allowance checks, and the vendored SafeERC20 transfer path. Tests covered unrelated standing approvals, front-run permits, no-op permits and silent fallbacks, empty/malformed revert data, no-return/false-return tokens, cross-token reentrancy, sum overflow, duplicates and sender recipients. Permit owner and transferFrom source are always msg.sender; callbacks cannot spend another caller's approval. No medium, high or critical findings were identified in this worker review; this is not an independent audit. Both imported informational findings reproduced, with none rejected: (1) src/Disperse.sol:52: a valid permit for 100 replaces an existing maximum allowance and the completed payout leaves allowance zero. This is intentional EIP-2612 behavior; use plain disperse when standing approval is sufficient, or account for its replacement. (2) src/Disperse.sol:92: a blocked second recipient reverts the entire batch, restoring earlier transfers, sender balance and allowance. This is intentional atomic behavior; simulate, identify/remove the refused row and retry. Neither warrants a source change under the approved unchanged implementation. Fee-on-transfer and rebasing tokens remain unsupported; callers must use trusted tokens, correct base-unit amounts and filtered recipients. Only zero and Disperse itself are rejected as recipients. Normal payouts transfer directly from caller to recipients; tokens sent directly to Disperse outside these functions cannot be recovered. Dispersed totals are requested amounts, not proof of receipt from a malicious token. No on-chain transaction was broadcast by this worker.
